title: The Alfiyya and its commentaries
summary: Ibn Mālik's thousand-verse poem of naḥw and ṣarf, the summit of the Arab and North-African path.

sections.heading: The poem
paragraphs: Ibn Mālik called it al-Khulāṣa al-alfiyya; it has about a thousand verses in the rajaz metre and covers naḥw and much of ṣarf. At least forty-three commentaries were written on it.
With al-Ājurrūmiyya it was among the first books memorised after the Qurʾān, and it is still taught in the pesantren of Indonesia and in Kerala.

sections.heading: Reading it
paragraphs: Most students read it with Ibn ʿAqīl's plain commentary; Ibn Hishām's Awḍaḥ al-masālik rearranges it in prose; and al-Ashmūnī's commentary is read by advanced students.

sources.title: Commentary of Ibn ʿAqīl on the Alfiyya, TAMIU OER
